correctness.rationale: Exact odd-part convention and global uniqueness are stated, all quantifiers k>=6 and zero-based indices fixed. An explicit 256-symbol length-16 factor histogram (64 distinct; 16x3,47x4,1x5) and length-7 parity separation support the short-factor base. Recursion x[2j]=1-(j mod2),x[2j+1]=x[j] transfers occurrences for longer factors, with one possible loss at a terminal source-suffix occurrence if the target ends with filler. A simultaneous induction proves every shorter factor has at least two occurrences and every shorter suffix at least three, removing the sole boundary hazard. Unique factors at the sharp odd length transfer bijectively by i→2i+1, giving exactly two and the closed formulas. Independent direct-counter and sorted-suffix programs were run from the package and reproduce bases and larger samples. Infinite theorem follows from proof, not experimental extrapolation.

originality.rationale: A 2026 general shortest-unique-substring algorithm has no uniform specialization for dyadic regular paperfolding prefixes. The most relevant 1992 paper by Allouche already proves the length-seven parity separation (credited, NOT presented as new) and the infinite-word factor-complexity count, but does not establish the multiplicity and positions of shortest unique factors in finite prefixes. A 2026 Thue–Morse classification concerns a non-equivalent automatic word. Actual searches of published indexed results and accessible prior ledgers revealed no same-object theorem. Priority risk remains for unindexed older literature; novelty is a best-evidence comparison, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Indexing may omit an earlier exact finite-prefix shortest unique factor classification for the regular paperfolding word.
The credited parity-rigidity lemma is not novel; the claim is only the exact finite-prefix threshold and two positions.
A generic algorithm can compute any fixed prefix; the claimed mathematical novelty rests on the closed all-k classification and proof, not basic computability.

value.rationale: Global shortest unique factors provide canonical signatures for finite sequences and matter in text indexing and alignment-free recognition. The exact invariant for every dyadic regular-paperfolding prefix is motivated independently of computation, includes precise locations and multiplicity rather than merely a count of distinct infinite-word factors, and the simultaneous suffix occurrence invariant explains why boundary deletion cannot spoil doubling. These are structural all-order results, not an arbitrary finite small-case census or a simple name change.
